subject: Re: Checkoutly: Queue backpressure causing token delays
messages:

Subject: Checkoutly: token delays and queuing observed

Hi Ben —

We started seeing elevated per-token delays across our checkout flows around 07:50 PST. Users get slower responses (3-8s per token vs typical ~0.3s), and our request queue is piling up in the client (we're dropping ~7% of requests due to timeouts). Attaching a few request ids and a short stack trace from our side.

Request ids: 2f9b1c, 2f9b1d, 2f9b20
Attached: backend-stacktrace.txt

Can your team confirm whether this is an infrastructure/backpressure problem on Redwood's end or something in our integration? We're in the middle of a Black Friday prep — this is high priority.

Alex — thanks for the quick heads-up and the traces. I'm escalating to SRE and product. Noted the request ids.

Quick context from our side: we observed an increase in queued model requests for tenant Checkoutly starting ~07:45 PST tied to a burst of long-context calls and a higher proportion of streaming completions. Typical causes: KV cache churn for streaming, batching misalignment creating backlog, or scheduling pressure on a handful of GPU workers.

I've looped in Soojin (oncall SRE) and Marissa (product lead for throughput tooling). Ben

--

ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Alex Perez <aperez@checkoutly.com>, Engineering Oncall <oncall@checkoutly.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:03:40 -0800
Subject: Re: Checkoutly: token delays and queuing observed

Ben / Alex —

Initial triage from infra: we see a short period of sustained high-concurrency graph across a subset of hosts serving the gen API for Checkoutly. Metrics: sustained concurrent requests per worker jumped ~6x for ~14 minutes. Observable symptoms: per-token scheduler latency increased, KV cache eviction rate spiked (prefix cache churn), and some long-running streaming RPCs held worker slots longer than expected.

Immediate mitigations we applied at 08:58 PST:
- Enabled per-tenant request throttling (soft cap) for Checkoutly to reduce queuing on affected workers.
- Temporarily lowered streaming chunk size for streaming endpoints to reduce time each connection holds a worker.
- Forced fallback routing for a fraction (~20%) of Checkoutly traffic to the dedicated overflow pool (smaller model family but lower tail latency).

Preliminary impact: queue depth halved within 3 minutes; per-token latency moved from high single-digit seconds to ~500-800ms for streaming cases. Non-streaming gen calls recovered faster (~120-200ms).

Next steps / asks for product and eng: 
1) Product: please sign off on continuing fallback routing for the next 4 hours and on a temporary conservative batching window for Checkoutly (50ms => 15ms).
2) Engineering: request a short-capacity bump (2 GPU-equivalents) into the dedicated overflow pool and a follow-up job to investigate KV churn root cause (likely tokenization fanout for long contexts).
3) Communication: we need a ~30 min customer-facing note acknowledging the incident and explaining mitigations + next steps. Ben, can you coordinate?

I've attached the backend stack trace and a short runtime dump. I'll open an INF ticket with traces.

-Soojin
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:12:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Checkoutly: Queue backpressure causing token delays

Thanks for the fast triage, Soojin. A few product-side asks and clarifications: 

- Sign-off: I approve continuing the fallback routing and reduced chunk sizes for 4 hours as a safety window.
- Batching window: lowering the batching window to 15ms could reduce latency but may increase per-token cost. We need explicit approval from the account team (Ben) to proceed on cost tradeoffs and for the capacity bump.
- Longer term: let's capture a quick postmortem focused on KV cache behavior and streaming worker lifecycle. I want a short list of possible mitigations we can prioritize (sticky KV per-tenant, more aggressive prefix caching, or a streaming worker pool that limits concurrent streaming connections).

Action items for eng/Product: 
* Karthik: lead the KV-churn investigation and propose 3 mitigations with estimated effort and perf impact by EOD tomorrow.
* Soojin: confirm whether the overflow routing instrumentation can auto-scale if we add capacity.
* Ben: draft customer note (short, calm, actionable) — highlight temporary fallback, expected improvement, and our ask to schedule a follow-up tech review.

I'll draft a short roadmap ticket for streaming-worker separation if Karthik's analysis points that way.

-Marissa
Director, Product (Throughput & Runtime)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Perez <aperez@checkoutly.com>, Marta Ruiz <mruiz@checkoutly.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Checkoutly: quick update on earlier token delays (what we changed)

Hi Alex / Marta —

Quick update from our side and next steps. First, apologies for the disruption this morning — we know this is bad timing with your upcoming traffic spike. We prioritized containment and took the following immediate actions to reduce user-visible latency: 

- Applied a soft per-tenant throttling cap to reduce request queueing.
- Reduced streaming chunk size to lower per-connection worker time.
- Routed ~20% of Checkoutly traffic to an overflow pool (smaller model family) to reduce tail latency.

Observed results: queue depth decreased ~50% within minutes and typical streaming per-token latency improved from multiple seconds to ~0.5-0.8s; non-streaming gen calls returned to ~150ms. We're continuing to monitor.

Next steps and asks from you: 
1) Can you confirm whether the reduced chunk size and temporary fallback materially impact your UX or costs on your end? If you can run a few smoke tests on staging (we've sent a flag to your tenant), that would be helpful.
2) We'd like to schedule a 45-minute technical review with your engineering team to walk through traces and the root-cause investigation. Proposed slots: Tue 10:00-10:45 PST or Tue 14:00-14:45 PST. Let me know which works.

As an immediate commitment, we're provisioning 2 GPU-equivalents into the overflow pool for the next 6 hours to keep latency stable while we dig deeper. I've attached a short capacity plan and a draft customer-facing note for your review.

We take this seriously — we'll follow up with a short incident summary and a proposed remediation roadmap after the root-cause analysis.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
